title: Resolve leaderboard misattribution caused by dynamic model naming churn
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We are seeing intermittent, tenant-specific leaderboard anomalies in the Console per-model top-N lists and heatmaps where model A briefly shows a drop and model B shows a spike that doesn't match real request patterns. Root cause analysis indicates this is caused by churn in dynamic model naming/aliasing during rollouts combined with non-idempotent backfill/retry paths in the streaming ingestion pipeline. Symptoms: (1) short-lived double-counting when late events from the old alias are ingested after alias swap, (2) 'negative reconciliation' rows in reconstructed hourly aggregates when backfill sweeps reassign events to a different alias, and (3) misleading burn-rate projections for customers because the top-model leaderboard temporarily includes the backfill pulse. Why this is new: rolling deploy cadence increased in the last quarter and we've introduced more aggressive alias-to-version mapping to support seamless rollouts; that uncovered a small-but-widespread class of misattribution when late/retied events lost provenance to their original model id. Business impact: customers see incorrect per-model cost breakdowns and may over/under-assign spend to product teams; observed impact on ~1.8% of active tenants during last week spike, several support tickets opened.
analysis_and_root_cause: Ingest pipeline currently relies on the incoming 'model_alias' field as the canonical attribution key. During alias swaps (canary -> stable), events that were produced under the previous alias can arrive out-of-order due to network retries/backfill jobs. When a backfill run replays older records without the original_model_fingerprint, the aggregator merges them under the current alias. Additionally, our rate-limit fanout implemention creates retry duplicates across shards when transient errors occur; those duplicates lack idempotency tokens and further exacerbate double-counting. The reconciliation stage applies a last-write-dedup strategy that assumes model identifiers are stable over the aggregation window — that assumption breaks under rapid alias churn and delayed ingest, producing corrective negative rows that confuse the console charts.
proposed_solution: 1) Event schema: add original_model_fingerprint and ingest_epoch fields at production time (producer SDK + gateway) so each event carries stable provenance separate from mutable alias. 2) Ingest processor: change dedup to use idempotency_token || original_model_fingerprint + request_id and respect ingest_epoch to segment backfills. 3) Reconstruct/backfill logic: tag reconstructed aggregates with provenance flags (live | backfill-epoch:<N>) and make backfill replays idempotent by default. 4) Console UX: surface 'freshness' bands in charts and add a toggle to exclude backfilled epochs; show provenance badges on top-N rows when attribution recovered. 5) Rollout: feature-flag the new fields, land producers and gateway changes first, then migrate aggregator in a canary with low-traffic tenants, run a dry backfill-rewrite job to back-populate fingerprints for 30 days window. 6) Monitoring: add reconciliation drift alert (percent of hourly rows with negative corrections > 0.5%) and a dashboard showing alias-swap frequency vs reconcile corrections.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Pros: will eliminate the majority of misattribution, make backfills safe and enable more transparent console UX. - Cons: schema change requires coordinated deploys (SDKs/gateways/producers), increases event size slightly, and the migration/backfill job will consume significant IO in initial run. - Risk: if we mis-handle epoch tagging we might fragment model timelines in the console; mitigate by preserving backward compatibility and normalizing display to collapse small epochs after 48 hours.
implementation_tasks: Add original_model_fingerprint and ingest_epoch producers SDK + gateway (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/producers/pull/409)
Update streaming deduper to use fingerprint + request_id (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/718)
Backfill-rewrite job that annotates recent 30d window with fingerprints and idempotency tokens (job: airflow/annotate-fingerprints-v1)
Aggregator migration: respect ingest_epoch and tag reconstructed rows with provenance flags
Console: add freshness band overlay and backfill filter toggle (design spec: https://drive.google.com/open?id=design-console-freshness)
Add reconciliation drift alert and runbook in PagerDuty playbooks
End-to-end integration tests and a canary run on 5 tenants for 48 hours
updates: 2025-02-03: Triage meeting (attendees: Aisha P., Marcus C., Lena R.). Pattern confirmed across three regions; ticket created.
2025-02-05: Spike test: replayed 24h of events with synthetic alias swaps; reproduced double-counting and negative reconciliation rows. (notes: /docs/spikes/alias-churn-repro.md)
2025-02-07: Prototype PR for producer SDK changes submitted (https://github.com/redwood-inference/producers/pull/409). Initial review by Lena R.: request to add unit tests for fingerprint generation.

2025-02-10: Ingest deduper patch landed in a feature branch. Bench: dedup lookup latency +1.2ms, memory +3% on p95 — acceptable for low-traffic canary. (benchmark: https://bench.redwood.ai/runs/2025-02-10/alias-dedupe)
2025-02-12: Design review for Console freshness UX completed; PM feedback: make backfill toggle default-off and expose a tooltip explaining 'backfill epochs'.
2025-02-14: Blocker identified: initial backfill-rewrite needs higher throughput than current Airflow workers; infra ticket created (ENG-135280) to scale workers for the migration job.
2025-02-15: QA plan drafted; small canary scheduled for 2025-02-18 on 5 pilot tenants. Post-canary, we'll run full 30d rewrite for tenants opted into the migration.
